### Managed care cut Medicaid costs [5.6%]{.accent} — but medical quality fell.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
library(plotly)
d <- read.csv("data/hero_aer2026.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
d$category <- factor(d$category, levels = d$category)
d$fill <- ifelse(d$category == "Total", "#b04a3f", "#00356B")
plot_ly(
  d, x = ~category, y = ~pct_change, type = "bar",
  marker = list(color = ~fill),
  hovertemplate = ~paste0(category, ": ", pct_change, "%<extra></extra>")
) |>
  layout(
    yaxis = list(title = "Cost change (%)", zeroline = TRUE, automargin = TRUE),
    xaxis = list(title = ""),
    margin = list(t = 10, l = 55),
    showlegend = FALSE
  ) |>
  config(displayModeBar = FALSE)
```

The savings came almost entirely from **pharmacy** management. Non-drug (medical) spending
changed little — outpatient costs fell modestly and inpatient was essentially flat — and
privatizing medical benefits was associated with **lower quality and satisfaction**.
:::
